name: sweeping the standing inventory
from: A standing memory inventory grown noisy by correct forward passes alone — additions accumulating faster than retirements: orphaned index lines, dangling files, oversized append-shaped journals wearing memory's frontmatter, clusters of hooks that sound alike.
to: The inventory matching its own rules: index and files agreeing one-to-one; append-shaped bodies moved to the research home with a one-fact pointer memory left in place under the same name; true duplicates merged only where one strictly subsumes the other; what was changed and what was deliberately left both reported. The sweep succeeds by making the inventory match its rules, not by shrinking it maximally.
cost: An occasional bounded pass over the whole standing inventory — every several sessions, or when the operator says it feels noisy — spent reading memory bodies before merging anything, because hooks that sound alike are evidence of nothing.
otherwise: The forward absorption step is not the same capacity as reconciling the backlog it leaves behind: each pass individually correct, the whole growing noisier, until recall degrades, real constraints get flattened into false duplicates, and the index approaches its truncation point silently.
